version.changelog:
Version 0.3.1

- Improved integration with external trackers (notably Plane) in scripts and issue creation workflows.
- Updated and expanded documentation in create.md and CHANGELOG.md.
- Removed legacy or redundant files (skill-card.md) for cleaner project organization.
- Refined client logic in scripts/plane_client.py and scripts/plane_create_issue.py for better external issue creation support.

llm.summary: This backlog skill includes high-impact Plane automation, automatic Kubernetes/Django-shell fallbacks, and a hardcoded private intake path that require careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The skill expects Plane API tokens, workspace profile data, local tracker files, optional kubeconfig/SSH access, and can mutate remote issue/page data or local markdown; that authority is broader than proportionate for a public backlog helper without tighter scoping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, service, hook, or startup persistence was found, but SKILL.md allows Bash(python3:*) and the Python scripts then invoke network requests, kubectl, ssh, and local file writes beyond the top-level allowed-tool framing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: create.md explicitly instructs automatic fallback from REST failures to kubectl exec into a Plane API pod; update/create scripts can run base64-decoded Python through manage.py shell without a separate opt-in approval gate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence was observed, but privileged effects can persist in Plane: database records are created or updated as the first superuser in fallback paths, and bulk/local scripts can rewrite tracker files or apply remote mutations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is broad vendor-agnostic backlog lifecycle management, but the artifact is heavily Plane-specific and includes issue/page creation, updates, comments, sync, pruning, bulk updates, and direct in-cluster Django ORM mutation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only in an environment where you intentionally grant Plane API access and Kubernetes/SSH admin access to the agent. Disable or remove the K3s/Django-shell fallbacks and the hardcoded intake.py private workspace path unless you explicitly need them and can audit every run. Prefer dry-run modes, require HTTPS-only endpoints, and verify the selected workspace, token source, and target project before allowing mutations.
llm.findings:
[T04] unexpected: Accepted: artifact/scripts/plane_create_entity.py, plane_create_issue.py, and plane_update_entity.py show automatic kubectl or ssh manage.py shell execution of generated base64 Python, which is a privileged application/database path beyond normal backlog REST operations.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: plane_update_entity.py fallback lookup can drop project/workspace constraints for issue sequence IDs, and intake.py uploads local backlog items to a hardcoded private Plane workspace when executed.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in part: plane_sync.py and plane_create_issue.py contain some transport hardening, but plane_client.py, plane_create_comment.py, plane_update_entity.py, intake.py, and plane_bulk_update.py still use urllib authenticated requests without equivalent HTTPS/redirect protections; bulk update also writes by default unless --dry-run is supplied.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md says proprietary tracker integrations are decoupled from the public core, while bundled scripts implement Plane-specific and K3s-specific workflows, including a private plane.dgs.ai.kr intake script.
[AS1] expected: Downgraded: the .gemini/config references in create.md and comment.md are directory probes for locating installed skill scripts, not evidence of reading agent configuration secrets.
[SC3] unexpected: Accepted: base64 wrapping appears to solve shell quoting, but it still reduces reviewability and enables dynamic code execution inside the Plane application pod.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: REST failure can trigger a privileged K3s/Django ORM fallback, so an authorization or configuration failure may be bypassed instead of failing closed.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: create.md discloses the fallback, but the top-level skill description and default capability summary do not make the privileged cluster execution prominent or opt-in.
